title: Samsung answers memory-capex race with fresh HBM capacity buildout by Q1 2027
body: By Q1 2027 Samsung — the one large memory maker absent from this week's capital surge — moves to match its rivals with a fresh, publicly-announced HBM or advanced-DRAM capacity commitment tied explicitly to AI demand. The trigger is the July 9 collision of two of the three big memory suppliers committing capital to the same bottleneck in the same week: Micron lifted its US manufacturing plan to more than $250 billion through 2035 (a $50 billion increase) and poured first concrete at its Clay, New York megafab a quarter ahead of schedule, while SK Hynix's record US listing earmarked proceeds for EUV-equipped capacity. With HBM stacks and advanced DRAM sold out well into the future and both rivals visibly locking in AI-era supply, Samsung faces direct competitive and customer-facing pressure to signal its own capacity path rather than cede the narrative. The predicted state change is a concrete Samsung commitment — a raised memory capex line, a new or expanded HBM/DRAM fab or line, or a formal AI-memory capacity target — announced through an earnings call, filing, or press release.

reasoning.because: Micron's $250B raise + NY concrete pour and SK Hynix's EUV-earmarked US listing hit the same week
reasoning.given: HBM and advanced DRAM are sold out ahead; two of three big memory makers committed fresh capital
reasoning.so_that: Samsung, the absent third supplier, announces a matching HBM/DRAM capacity commitment or raised memory capex
reasoning.landing: By Q1 2027; ≥1 Samsung capacity or capex announcement tied to AI memory demand
reasoning.plain_language: Two of the three big memory-chip makers just poured money into AI memory in one week; expect the third, Samsung, to follow soon.

summary: After Micron raised its US plan past $250 billion and SK Hynix's record listing earmarked EUV capacity in the same week, Samsung is the one large memory maker yet to commit fresh AI-memory capital. By Q1 2027 it likely answers with a new HBM or DRAM capacity commitment or raised memory capex.
